title: Daisy reports permissions as missing when they are already granted
description:
What happens On launch, Daisy shows Accessibility and Input Monitoring as missing and will not start the listener, even though Daisy is already switched on in System Settings → Privacy & Security. Requesting again does nothing. The only way out is to remove Daisy from both lists and grant it again, or re-add the app by hand. Likely cause macOS ties these permissions to the app's code signature, not its name. A build signed differently (for example a local Apple Development build versus the Developer ID release, or an older build) shows up as "Daisy" in System Settings but does not count for the running app. Daisy then sees no permission and blocks Start. Expected - Daisy does not refuse to start on a pre-check that can be wrong; it starts and reports what actually fails.
- When a permission is missing but Daisy appears in the list, Daisy says the entry belongs to another copy and offers to fix it (remove and re-add), instead of looping on requests.
- Input Monitoring granted while Daisy is running is picked up, with a relaunch if macOS requires one. Affected Daisy 0.1.0 and 0.1.1.
acceptance_criteria: Daisy starts with valid permissions on a clean install and after an upgrade from 0.1.1; a stale entry from another signature is detected and explained with a fix; no remove-and-re-add loop. Verified on hardware with the release build.
notes: GitHub: https://github.com/misfitdev/daisy/issues/6

title: Control follows whichever Mac you are using
description:
## Summary

Remove Host/Guest and Wait/Connect from the interface. Whichever Mac has hands on its keyboard or trackpad drives; the other follows. Moving to the other Mac and using it hands control over automatically, and the screen arrangement stays the same, because the layout is stored as one relation both Macs share ("A's right edge meets B") rather than as per-Mac roles.

## Behavior

- Both Macs watch their own input at all times. Physical input (not input Daisy posted) on a Mac makes it the driver: it sends a claim, the other Mac releases what it holds and follows.
- Local input always wins: touching a Mac's own keyboard or trackpad returns control to it immediately.
- A short settle window prevents control flapping when both Macs are used at once.
- Setup is: pair, then say which side the other Mac sits on. Status names the other Mac ("Connected to …"), not roles.
- With Bonjour, both Macs advertise and the pair agrees deterministically who opens the connection; Wait for a peer / Connect by Address leave the default UI (typing an address stays available for networks Bonjour does not reach).

## Consequences

- Every Mac needs both Accessibility and Input Monitoring; the role-aware permission rule from #11 is simplified.
- Protocol: messages to claim control and to agree on the shared layout (appended variants).
- Swipe capture still requires macOS 27 on the Mac in use.
acceptance_criteria: No Host/Guest or Wait/Connect choice in the default UI. Using either Mac's keyboard or trackpad makes it the driver within one event, with the arrangement unchanged; local input always wins; no flapping with brief simultaneous use. Handoff and layout agreement are unit tested; verified on two Macs with each macOS version recorded.
notes: GitHub: https://github.com/misfitdev/daisy/issues/13

title: Install from a DMG and walk through permissions on first launch
description:
Getting Daisy running takes too many manual steps: unzip, move to Applications, find two System Settings panes. macOS only lets the user grant Accessibility and Input Monitoring in System Settings, so no installer can do it; the app has to guide it.

1. DMG: just package also builds Daisy-<version>-macos-arm64.dmg with Daisy.app and an Applications shortcut, signed, notarized and stapled like the zip. release.yml uploads it with its .sha256, attestation and SLSA provenance. Site Download page and docs/usage.md point to the DMG.
2. Self-move: launched from outside /Applications (Downloads, a mounted DMG, App Translocation), Daisy offers to move itself to /Applications and relaunch from there; declining keeps running. Handles an existing copy in /Applications (replace, keeping settings) and a read-only source.
3. Permission walkthrough: on first launch, and whenever a permission is missing, a step-by-step window triggers each system prompt (Accessibility, then Input Monitoring), opens the exact System Settings pane (x-apple.systempreferences deep links), polls, and advances once each permission turns on. Input Monitoring often applies only after a relaunch: offer Relaunch Daisy. Then continue to pairing.
acceptance_criteria: The DMG is notarized and stapled (spctl -a -t open --context context:primary-signature and stapler validate pass) and published by the release workflow with attestation and provenance. Opening Daisy from the DMG or Downloads offers to move it and relaunches from /Applications. On a Mac with neither permission granted, the walkthrough reaches pairing with both granted without the user searching System Settings. Decisions (location check, step state) are unit tested; install and permissions verified on hardware, recording macOS version.

title: Per-Mac trust policies and forced revocation
description:
Trust is forever today: a Mac paired once, long ago, can connect and take   
over the keyboard at any time. Make trust a policy chosen per Mac, expiring 
by default.                                                                 
                                                                            
Policies:                                                                   
                                                                            
• Idle limit, the default: trust ends after 96 hours without an             
authenticated session with that Mac. Refreshed while connected, at least    
every heartbeat interval, so a pair that stays connected never expires.     
• For N days: a hard deadline N days after pairing, however often the Macs  
connect. Being connected does not extend it.                                
• Just this once: the key is kept in memory only and trust ends with the    
session. After an unexpected drop, the same key may reconnect without a code
for 60 seconds; after a deliberate disconnect, never.                       
• Forever: never expires until forgotten. Always shown as such, since it is 
the one that brings back the original risk.                                 
                                                                            
Rules:                                                                      
                                                                            
• Each Mac enforces its own policy for the other, with its own clock. Trust 
needs both sides, so the stricter policy wins and a peer cannot override    
this Mac's choice by claiming it still trusts us.                           
• Expired trust means unpaired: refuse the Mac, drop its stored key, and    
require pairing again with a code.                                          
• Choose a policy when pairing (--trust idle|<N>d|once|forever), change it
later (daisy trust  ...), and in the menu bar app.                      
• The peers file becomes structured, holding key, name, paired at, last seen
and policy; existing pairs migrate to the default.                          
• daisy peers and the menu bar show each Mac's policy and time remaining.
• Also offer rotating this Mac's own identity key, which makes every paired 
Mac pair again.                                                             
                                                                            
Revocation, forced and immediate:
- Remove trust for one Mac, several at once, or all of them: daisy forget <mac>..., daisy forget --all, and the same in the menu bar app.
- A revoked Mac is cut off at once: any live session with it ends, and in-memory trust from "just this once" and any open grace window are dropped.
- Revocation reaches the running app, and a running process must never write back a stale peer list that restores a revoked Mac. Today the running app saves its whole in-memory list when it pairs, which can undo a forget made from another terminal.

Tests: each policy expires exactly when it should; an active session keeps  
an idle-limit pin fresh but not a deadline; the grace window applies only   
after an unexpected drop, only for the same key, and only for 60 seconds; a 
peer claiming trust cannot override an expired local policy.                



BLOCKS
← ○ mn-9gq: Discover paired Macs with Bonjour ● P2
← ○ mn-e3p: Reconnect after sleep, wake and network changes ● P2
← ○ mn-075: Menu bar app that sets up and controls the connection ● P1
close_reason: Per-Mac policies (idle, Nd, once with a 60 second grace after a dropped connection, forever), forget for one, many or all Macs that ends live sessions within a second, a locked peers.toml that running processes cannot overwrite, and rotate-key. Verified end to end on loopback with a real driving session.

title: Menu bar app that sets up and controls the connection
description:
Ends the beta. A menu bar app that needs the terminal for setup is no use, so the app configures the connection itself.

- Restructure: AppKit on the main thread, the async runtime on background threads, talking over channels. The event tap keeps its own thread.
- Connection setup: add a Mac by name or address, choose driving or following and which side the other Mac sits on, list and forget paired Macs, saved to a settings file.
- Pairing in the app: show the code on one Mac, enter it on the other, driving the same SPAKE2 flow as the CLI.
- Trust renewal: when a Mac's trust has expired (see the trust lifecycle issue), say so and walk through pairing again.
- Status icon (connected, waiting, disconnected), connect and disconnect, quit, and launch at login with SMAppService.
- First-run onboarding: grant Accessibility and Input Monitoring, then pair.
acceptance_criteria: A signed menu-bar application can start and stop listen/connect sessions, initiate pairing, show connection and permission state, manage trusted peers, and surface actionable errors without requiring terminal commands; unit tests and two-Mac hardware verification pass.
notes:
Revocation through control channel: forgetting trust from the menu-bar UI aborts the active session immediately; peer-file watching remains the external-edit backstop. Implemented native AppKit menu-bar UI, first-run setup window, permission actions, pairing prompts, paired-Mac trust/forget menus, SMAppService launch at login, color-only Daisy status icon, background Tokio controller, atomic 0600 settings, and shared CLI/UI service orchestration. Signed bundle was built and visually inspected on this Mac; conditional connection and control fields were exercised. just check and dependency/workflow security gates pass. Remaining acceptance work: run the signed app on two Macs and verify start/stop listen/connect, pairing on both sides, live revocation, permission-state recovery, keyboard/mouse control and hardware swipe behavior in this session before closing.
Impeccable finish verdict: ship. Follow-up fixes resolved recovery-chord visibility, pairing-window status drift, listener post-disconnect state, control accessibility labels, concise recoverable error presentation, two-second permission refresh/action gating, and missing Daisy bundle icon. just check passes 143 tests with 1 ignored; strict code-sign verification and all security/workflow gates pass. Bead remains open solely for required two-Mac live verification (including connected-yellow status, pairing/revocation, input/swipes/recovery chord and denied-permission paths).
2026-09-26: Redesigned the native setup window as an intentional AppKit Operate surface. Connection is primary; Role is a subordinate Host/Guest choice with concise helper copy, dynamic conditional layout, a status-aware Daisy header, a dedicated Permissions section, hidden granted-permission actions, and active/inactive action-state cleanup. Updated README, usage, security, PRODUCT, and DESIGN language and mapped role mismatch recovery to Host/Guest. Visually inspected Wait/Connect x Host/Guest in an isolated signed preview. just check passed (144 tests), the final bundle built, and strict codesign verification passed. Two-Mac setup and control flow remains outstanding; keep mn-075 open.
2026-09-26: Corrected the setup-window header mark to keep its yellow brand center regardless of connection state. Gray/yellow status changes remain exclusive to the menu-bar glyph. Rebuilt with the established Apple Development identity; just check and strict codesign verification passed.
2026-09-26: Reworked the setup window using the approved reference direction: adaptive rounded Connection and Permissions groups, direct segmented controls for connection and Host/Guest, native menus for longer choices, a restrained coral Connection rule, and a coral primary action that shifts from Pair to Start once peers exist. Updated DESIGN.md. Visually inspected waiting/connecting layouts and accessibility roles in isolated signed builds. just check passed (144 tests total: 143 passed, 1 ignored, plus the main test), final bundle built, and strict codesign verification passed.

title: Discover paired Macs with Bonjour
description:
Find paired Macs on the local network with Bonjour (mDNS-SD), so the connecting menu-bar app does not need a name or address.

- A Do Not Broadcast setting turns advertising off entirely; connections by name or address only. Keep manual addresses working for routed networks.
- Advertise only while listening, and reveal no Mac name or key in the advertisement.
- Offer only paired Macs whose trust has not expired, apart from pairing mode.
acceptance_criteria: Daisy advertises and discovers compatible peers with Bonjour, validates service metadata, handles duplicate names and network changes, lets the user select an address without manual hostname entry, and passes unit plus two-Mac network tests.

title: Daisy: many-to-many control across a group of Macs with a shared layout
description:
Grow from one pair of Macs into a group of Macs that share input as one desk. Today Daisy is strictly two Macs: the listener serves one connection at a time (src/main.rs accept loop awaits each session), each process has one peer on one edge (`--drive <side>`, a single `Side` in input.rs), and trust is pairwise only. The name Daisy comes from this idea: Macs chained edge to edge.

What it looks like to the user: arrange any number of Macs in a layout in the menu bar app, push the pointer off any screen edge and land on whichever Mac is there, as if it were one big desktop. Adding a Mac is pairing with any Mac already in the group.

Pre-planning only. Decompose into child issues and plan before building.
design:
Decisions made so far (2026-09-26):

1. Many-to-many, one controller per Mac. Any Mac can drive; a Mac is controlled by at most one other Mac at a time. HID control is enforced: the Mac whose physical keyboard/trackpad is in use holds control of the target, and a second driver cannot take a Mac already being controlled.

2. Shared layout in one global coordinate space. Every Mac's display(s) are rectangles with X/Y origin and size in a single global space. The layout is defined and edited dynamically in the control UX (menu bar app, mn-075) and distributed to every node, so each Mac knows where it sits by geometry. Edge crossing becomes "which rectangle does the pointer enter next", replacing the single `Side` model. Layout changes must be versioned so nodes agree on one layout; a stale layout must not route input.

3. Star topology with a coordinator, presented as a chain. The Mac in use coordinates and holds a direct session to every Mac in the group. When C joins through B (C connects to B, the Mac it knows), B introduces C and redirects it to the coordinator; C connects directly to A and is placed in the layout relative to B. To the user it looks like a daisy chain; on the wire it is a star. No hop re-injects input: a relaying Mac would have to re-capture injected events through its own event tap, which tangles pointer pinning and held-input release.

4. Transitive (introduced) trust. Accepted change to the security model: "I trust you and you trust them, so they inherit your trust." Mechanism: signed introductions. The introducer signs C's public key, trust policy and expiry; members accept it because they trust the introducer. Requirements:
   - Signed revocations propagate to every member; forgetting a Mac also revokes everything it introduced.
   - Stricter policy still wins: an introduced Mac's trust cannot outlive its introducer's.
   - A compromised member can admit a new Mac; docs/security-model.md must be rewritten to state this.
   - Short codes remain PAKE input only; never displayed for visual comparison.

5. Group stays awake; automatic re-establishment. While the group is active, every Mac holds a power assertion against idle system sleep (IOPMAssertion); displays may still dim. When control enters a Mac, declare user activity (IOPMAssertionDeclareUserActivity) to wake its display. Coordinate nap and wake across the group. If a Mac does sleep, it rejoins automatically once awake and unlocked, provided its trust is still inside its window and the trust keys have not been offline past the point where they can be refreshed. Unlock cannot be done across the group: the lock screen uses secure input and ignores posted events, so each Mac is unlocked locally (Touch ID); the coordinator shows which Macs are locked. Do not change the user's lock settings. Overlaps mn-e3p (reconnect after sleep).

6. Latency is measured, not assumed. Add round-trip instrumentation (no clock sync needed) with p50/p99 histograms, surfaced as a stats command and in the app. Record in microseconds; network jitter dwarfs nanosecond resolution. Expected: tens of microseconds for capture/encrypt/send, ~100-300 us per wired gigabit hop, 1-5 ms per Wi-Fi hop with 10-50+ ms spikes. Wi-Fi hops, not processing, dominate.

Stretch goals (stay stretch even after building starts):
- Pass-through when direct fails: if C cannot reach the coordinator directly (subnet, firewall), B forwards opaque bytes. The Noise session stays end to end between coordinator and C, so B cannot read or inject. Costs one hop.
- Coordinator handoff: whichever Mac's hardware is in use becomes coordinator, seamlessly, since every node holds the layout. Only if it can be done without visible interruption.

Constraints from AGENTS.md: protocol::Message and InputEvent are encoded by variant position, so new messages are appended only. The event tap callback must stay nonblocking; layout lookups it needs are cached.
acceptance_criteria: Done when (merged from mn-8ck): users arrange multiple trusted Macs spatially and move control through configured edges on any side with no loops or ambiguous ownership; control can be recovered locally from any node; the connected topology and failures are clearly visible; deterministic tests plus multi-Mac hardware verification pass; protocol compatibility and practical peer limits are documented. Until implemented, product copy and brand may anticipate this topology but must label it planned.
notes: Status: pre-planning, not building. Needs decomposition and planning before any code.

title: Support positioned multi-Mac daisy chains
description: Extend Daisy beyond a single pairwise session so users can position multiple trusted Macs around the driving Mac and move through chained connections across left, right, above, and below edges. The brand may anticipate this topology, but product copy must label it planned until implemented.
acceptance_criteria: Users can arrange multiple trusted Macs spatially, move control through configured edges without loops or ambiguous ownership, recover locally from any node, observe clear connected topology and failures, and pass deterministic plus multi-Mac hardware verification; protocol compatibility and practical peer limits are documented.

title: Use the Daisy name everywhere
description: Use Daisy as the only name across the repository and the product: crate, binary and app bundle (dev.misfit.daisy), data directory, environment variables, protocol labels, docs, website, workflows and tooling configuration.
acceptance_criteria: Every naming surface is inventoried and intentionally migrated or retained for compatibility; user data and pairing identities survive upgrade; docs, packaging, release workflows, tests, and security guidance use the approved name; old-name compatibility and deprecation behavior are documented.
close_reason: Daisy is the only name in the repository: crate and binary daisy, Daisy.app with bundle ID dev.misfit.daisy, data in ~/Library/Application Support/daisy, DAISY_* environment variables, protocol labels daisy/1 and 'daisy pairing v1', docs, website (base /daisy, repo links misfitdev/daisy), workflows, tooling config and issue text. No migration from old installs. The GitHub repo and local folder keep their current names until the new repo is created.

title: Define Daisy brand identity
description: Create the first durable visual identity for Daisy using the Impeccable new-world workflow. The identity must express a simple, open-ended daisy chain of many Macs without changing the separately managed website implementation.
acceptance_criteria: User approves a distinctive brand direction grounded in Daisy product truth; approved identity is documented in DESIGN.md and .impeccable/design.json; generated raster assets retain prompt provenance; website implementation remains untouched.
notes:
Current scope is identity only; repository-wide language migration is deferred. Approved direction preserves a quiet off-white board, side-by-side many-Mac demonstration, centered Daisy nodes, restrained coral editorial accents, connected yellow centers, and matte anodized-gray chain links. Chain grammar uses overlapping fixed-size subset and superset U links, never stretched cables. Curved U bowls face the flower in horizontal, vertical, and diagonal orientations. Menu-bar connected state is a gray flower with yellow center; disconnected is the identical all-gray flower, with no side-link ears. App icon direction is one larger centered Daisy bloom without side links. Final art may be fine-tuned during production. This latest board is the stamp candidate pending explicit approval.
Approved by user through the decision board. Final amendment: chain paths may bend and flow at angles like a physical chain; each turn rotates whole fixed-size links, preserving overlap and bowl direction, with no stretching or smooth cable substitution.
close_reason: Daisy identity approved and stamped into DESIGN.md and .impeccable/design.json; approved comp and prompt provenance recorded.

title: Initialize durable Impeccable product context
description: Update the existing PRODUCT.md through the Impeccable init workflow so it records confirmed Daisy product truth, uses a supported platform value, and does not interfere with the separately managed website session.
acceptance_criteria: PRODUCT.md follows schema 1 with a supported platform value; only user-confirmed durable product facts are retained; website work remains untouched; product context loads without the platform warning.
close_reason: PRODUCT.md repaired and confirmed as the shared product record; Codex image generation enabled through the Impeccable comp-first workflow configuration.

title: Add ReachSec to mise
description: Pin and install ReachSec through the repository mise configuration alongside cargo-audit, then run it against the current Rust dependency graph and record any findings.
acceptance_criteria: mise resolves and installs a pinned ReachSec version; reachsec reports its version; a repository scan runs or an exact blocker is recorded; just check remains green.
notes: Pinned ReachSec 0.1.0 source at 548b228ba35774664d4d691b6fddf537aa6225db. Its postinstall provisions nightly-2025-08-09 with rust-src/rustc-dev/llvm-tools-preview and installs the full cg4rs package at ReachSec's pinned submodule revision b6cdc5f38410a934789ab70f2b8a41eaae2529ef. mise install --dry-run: all tools installed. title: Configure cargo-deny and resolve atomic-polyfill advisory
description: cargo-deny 0.20.2 is now available through mise, but a full cargo deny check has no repository policy: licenses are rejected by default and advisories flag RUSTSEC-2023-0089 for atomic-polyfill 1.0.3 via postcard/heapless. Define an intentional deny.toml policy and remove, upgrade, or explicitly document the unmaintained dependency.
acceptance_criteria: cargo deny check exits zero under a reviewed repository policy; RUSTSEC-2023-0089 is removed or has an explicit documented exception with owner and review date.
notes: Set postcard default-features=false while retaining use-std, removing unused heapless/atomic-polyfill dependency and RUSTSEC-2023-0089. Added deny.toml with explicit license, duplicate-version, wildcard, registry, and git-source policy. cargo deny check, cargo audit, reachsec check, and just check all exit 0.
close_reason: cargo-deny policy passes and atomic-polyfill removed from dependency graph

acceptance_criteria: mise configuration declares the supported scanners; mise installs/resolves them; each scanner reports a version; relevant local scans are executed or exact blockers recorded.

title: Share copied images
description: Send copied images (PNG, TIFF) across using the chunked transfer from text sharing. Images can be tens of megabytes: cap the size, prefer PNG over TIFF to keep transfers small, and avoid holding several copies in memory.
acceptance_criteria: Supported image clipboard formats synchronize both directions with a documented size cap and preferred compact representation, without feedback loops or redundant copies, and pass deterministic plus two-Mac tests.
notes: Implemented 2026-09-27: protocol Clipboard{part} (tag 10) with Begin/Chunk/End/Done parts; pure src/clipboard.rs (Outbox/Inbox/Sharing, limits 4 MiB text/rtf, 32 MiB png, 60,000-byte chunks, echo prevention by change count); share.rs sends on crossing (driver after Enter, follower after Leave/Reclaim) through a lower-priority snapshot queue; src/macos/pasteboard.rs (TIFF to PNG); Share Clipboard menu toggle and --no-clipboard CLI flag; docs updated. just check passes, mutation-checked. Remaining: two-Mac hardware verification (record Macs and macOS versions), then flip README/PRODUCT/site status to working.
close_reason: Clipboard sharing implemented: text, rich text and images (TIFF to PNG) travel when control crosses, both ways; 4 MB text / 32 MB image limits; chunked Clipboard protocol messages sent behind input and heartbeats; echo prevention; Share Clipboard toggle (on by default) and --no-clipboard. just check passes. Hardware problems will be filed as bugs.

title: Share copied text and rich text
description: Watch NSPasteboard changeCount on both Macs and send plain text with its rich forms (RTF, HTML) to the other Mac, which puts the same types on its pasteboard. Builds what images and files reuse: splitting messages larger than one frame (65,519 bytes) and reassembling them, a size cap, and not echoing back a copy that just arrived. Never send items marked org.nspasteboard.ConcealedType or TransientType, which password managers use, so copied passwords stay on their Mac.
acceptance_criteria: Plain text and supported rich-text clipboard formats synchronize both directions without feedback loops, enforce a documented size cap, reject malformed or oversized payloads, and pass deterministic plus two-Mac tests.

title: Controlled swipes that follow the fingers
description: Forward every captured swipe step—phase, progress, ending velocity, and cancellation—while keeping a swipe on the Mac that had control when it began. macOS 27 followers replay through a 16 ms pacer with stale-progress coalescing; macOS 26 followers use the shortcut fallback. End-to-end hardware verification covers live progress, pullback, cancellation, completion, Spaces, Mission Control, application windows, and the macOS 26 regression path.
acceptance_criteria: Real-trackpad end-to-end testing verifies live macOS 27 swipe replay follows progress, pullback, cancellation, and completion for Spaces, Mission Control, and application windows; macOS 26 shortcut fallback regression is verified; automated tests remain green.
notes: Implementation and verification complete. The driver forwards InputEvent::Swipe steps; the macOS 27 follower paces live IOHID replay and cancels an unfinished swipe when control or the session leaves; macOS 26 recognizes direction and invokes the configured shortcut. Synthetic direction behavior was measured on hardware and pinned in tests. 2026-09-26 hardware verification completed the real-trackpad macOS 27 follower path and macOS 26 fallback regression.
close_reason: Controlled swipe replay and macOS 26 fallback verified end to end on hardware

title: Reconnect after sleep, wake and network changes
description: Reconnect after sleep, wake and network changes without being asked, within the trust lifecycle: only to paired Macs whose trust has not expired, and never by pairing silently. When trust expires, stop reconnecting and ask for pairing again. Detect dropped sessions promptly.
acceptance_criteria: Trusted sessions recover after sleep, wake, interface changes, and transient disconnects with bounded backoff; deliberate stop, forget, trust expiry, and invalid identity never reconnect; behavior is covered by deterministic tests and two-Mac hardware verification.
notes: Implemented 2026-09-28: service::connect loops: connect (5 s timeout), Noise handshake, key must match the Mac of the first session (reconnect::KeyChanged stops), trust check, run session; on drop waits via backon exponential backoff (1,2,4,8 s then 10 s, jitter; resets after a 30 s session); retries only network failures (reconnect::retryable); reconnects never pair. Listener side already re-accepts. Status::Reconnecting in app and CLI. Docs updated. just check passes (176), cargo deny/audit pass with backon; loop rules mutation-checked. Remaining: two-Mac verification of sleep/wake and Wi-Fi change (record Macs and macOS versions), then flip README/site status.
close_reason: Reconnect implemented: connecting Mac retries network failures with backon backoff (1,2,4,8 s then 10 s, jittered), redoes the Noise handshake and trust check each time, stops on trust, key-change or setup failures, never pairs on reconnect; Reconnecting status in app and CLI; docs updated. just check passes (176 tests). Hardware problems will be filed as bugs.

title: Limit pairing attempts
description: Each connection in pairing mode is one online guess at a 6 digit code. Cap attempts per window and end pairing mode after a success or a timeout.
close_reason: Pairing now permits at most five unknown-key attempts for ten minutes, closes after success, and bounds handshake/trust waits; regression tests and just check passed.

title: Share the clipboard
description: Copy on one Mac and paste on the other, for the kinds of content people copy. Split into text and rich text, images, and files; text and rich text comes first because it builds the sync the others share.
acceptance_criteria: Text/rich text, images, and files are implemented through the child issues with bounded sizes, encrypted transport, loop prevention, platform-appropriate fidelity, tests, documentation, and two-Mac verification.

title: Forward scrolling with phase and momentum
description: Forward continuous scroll deltas plus kCGScrollWheelEventScrollPhase and MomentumPhase so trackpad scrolling stays smooth, instead of wheel ticks.
acceptance_criteria: Scroll deltas, phase, and momentum phase are preserved end to end without stuck or duplicated momentum; mouse-wheel behavior remains correct; captured hardware conventions are pinned in tests and verified between two Macs.
notes: 2026-09-26: Removed public documentation language describing scroll phase/momentum as a limitation or planned feature to avoid confusing users. This does not assert hardware validation and does not close the issue; implementation and validation can be revisited later.

title: Verify shake-to-locate on a macOS 26 follower
description:
## Steps to Reproduce
1. Enable Accessibility > Display > Pointer > Shake mouse pointer to locate on a macOS 26 following Mac.
2. Control it from a paired driving Mac.
3. Shake the physical mouse or trackpad pointer rapidly.
4. Observe whether Daisy enlarges the follower pointer and restores its configured size afterward.

The synthetic-event limitation is confirmed and the replay-side detector plus CGSSetCursorScale implementation is verified on macOS 27. The remaining work is macOS 26 visual and cleanup-path verification.
acceptance_criteria: On a macOS 26 follower with Shake to locate enabled, a real end-to-end shake visibly enlarges the pointer and restores the configured size after shaking, session exit, and next launch after forced termination; disabling the system setting suppresses enlargement; the tested versions are recorded.
notes:
2026-09-25: Added tools/probe-shake.swift, a CGEventPost(.cghidEventTap) synthetic oscillation matching the injector's source, location and delta fields. swiftc -typecheck and just check pass on local macOS 27.0. No visual observation yet: local screen capture fails ('could not create image from rect'), so the positive-control real shake and synthetic shake must be compared on the receiving Mac with Shake mouse pointer to locate enabled before choosing an implementation.
Cause confirmed by measurement: CGSGetCursorScale stays 1.0 through 200 synthetic shake events on macOS 27 with Shake to locate on. Implemented: src/shake.rs detects the shake in replayed motion; src/macos/pointer.rs grows the pointer to 4x with CGSSetCursorScale and eases back. Verified on macOS 27 through the real Injector: scale rose to 4.0 and returned to 1.0; after kill -9 mid-shake it stayed 4.0 and the next start restored 1.0. tools/probe-shake.swift removed as superseded. Remaining: visual check on the macOS 26 follower.

title: Store the identity key in the Keychain
description: The private key is a 0600 file today; the login Keychain would protect it better.
acceptance_criteria: The long-term private key is created and loaded from the login Keychain with least-privilege access; existing file keys migrate without identity rotation or permission regression; failures are explicit and tests cover migration and refusal paths.

title: Website: the page is the desk; push the browser edge to move between screens
description:
Explore a landing page where each section is a Mac screen on a desk and the visitor moves between them by pushing the real mouse against the browser edge, the way Daisy moves control between Macs. Shelved during mn-1pb in favor of the in-page desk simulation; worth revisiting for fun.

Notes from the discussion: a maximized browser stops the pointer at the display edge, so crossing must be detected as a push (pointer held at the edge while moving outward), not a mouseleave. Arrow keys and a small screen map as alternatives; phones and reduced motion fall back to the vertical page. Open questions: home only or whole site; fixed row, all four edges, or a visitor-arrangeable layout; whether the in-page desk simulation stays.
acceptance_criteria: A future design spike documents the push-at-edge interaction, keyboard and touch fallbacks, reduced-motion behavior, scope across the site, and a browser-tested prototype or a recorded decision not to pursue it.

title: Share copied files
description: Lowest priority; may not land. Copying files in Finder and pasting on the other Mac. Transfer the contents with progress and cancellation, and put the received files on the pasteboard, as file promises or from a temporary folder that is cleaned up. Handle folders and a size cap. A paired Mac can send any file, so quarantine received files like downloads.
acceptance_criteria: Copied files synchronize with explicit size/count limits, safe filenames and destinations, no path traversal or partial-file exposure, clear failure reporting, and deterministic plus two-Mac tests.
